questions.q:
Statement-I : Two forces \left(\overset{→}{P} + \overset{→}{Q}\right)$ and \left(\overset{→}{P} - \overset{→}{Q}\right)$ where $\overset{→}{P} ⊥ \overset{→}{Q},$~when act at an angle ${θ}_{1}$ each other, the magnitude of their resultant is $\sqrt{3\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right)},$~when they act at an angle ${θ}_{2},$~the~magnitude of their resultant becomes $\sqrt{2\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right)} .$~This is possible only when ${θ}_{1} < {θ}_{2} .$
Statement-II : In the situation given above.
${θ}_{1} = 60 °$~and~${θ}_{2} = 90 °$
In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I& is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I& is true but Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{F}1$ and $\overset{→}{F}2$ at ${θ}_{1}$
${F}_{net1} = \sqrt{P^{2} + Q^{2} + P^{2} + Q^{2} + 2\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right)cos{θ}_{1}}$
${F}_{net2} = \sqrt{P^{2} + Q^{2} + P^{2} + Q^{2} + 2\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right)cos{θ}_{2}}$
If ${F}_{net1} = \sqrt{3\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right)} = \sqrt{2\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right) + 2\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right)cos{θ}_{1}}$
$⇒ cos{θ}_{1} = \dfrac{P^{2} + Q^{2}}{2\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right)}$
$⇒ {θ}_{1} = 60 °$
${F}_{net2} = \sqrt{2\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right)} = \sqrt{2\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right) + 2\left(P^{2} + Q^{2}\right)cos{θ}_{2}}$
$⇒ cos{θ}_{2} = 0 ⇒ {θ}_{2} = 90 °$

questions.q: A physical quantity $P$ is given as~$P = \dfrac{a^{2}b^{3}}{c\sqrt{d}}$.~The percentage error in the measurement of $a, b, c$ and $d$ are $1 % , 2 % , 3 %$ and $4 %$ respectively. The percentage error in the measurement of quantity $P$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given quantity is& $P = \dfrac{a^{2}b^{3}}{c\sqrt{d}}$.

The percentage error for a quantity can be given by the formula~$\dfrac{∆ x}{x} \times 100$.

Relation of the relative errors will be,

\left(\dfrac{\Delta P}{P}\right) = \left[\left(\dfrac{2\Deltaa}{a}\right) + \left(\dfrac{3\Deltab}{b}\right) + \left(\dfrac{\Deltac}{c}\right) +\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\Deltad}{d}\right)\right]

Hence, the percentage error is calculated by substituting the values,

\left(\dfrac{\Delta P}{P}\right) \times$100 = \left($2 $\times$1\right) + \left($3 $\times$2\right) + 3 + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times$4\right) = 13 %$.

$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$V = \dfrac{\pid^{2}h}{4} = \dfrac{π}{4}\left(12.6\right)2\left(34.2\right)cm^{3}$

$\dfrac{dV}{V} = \dfrac{2d\left(d\right)}{d} + \dfrac{d\left(h\right)}{h}$

Converting to errors

$\dfrac{∆ V}{V} = 2\dfrac{∆ d}{d} + \dfrac{∆ h}{h}$

$\dfrac{∆ V}{4260} = 2 \left(\dfrac{0.1}{12.6}\right) +\left(\dfrac{0.1}{34.2}\right)

$⇒ ∆ V = 80cm^{3}$

$V = 4260 $\pm$80cm^{3}

questions.q: Two vectors $\overset{→}{P}$ and $\overset{→}{Q}$ have equal magnitudes. If the magnitude of $\overset{→}{P} + \overset{→}{Q}$ is $n$ times the magnitude of $\overset{→}{P} - \overset{→}{Q},$~then angle between $\overset{→}{P}$ and $\overset{→}{Q}$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$| \overset{→}{P} | = | \overset{→}{Q} | = x \ldots \left(i\right)$

$| \overset{→}{P} + \overset{→}{Q} | = n | \overset{→}{P} - \overset{→}{Q} |$

$P^{2} + Q^{2} + 2PQcos\theta =n^{2} \left($P^{2} + Q^{2} - $2PQcos\theta\right)

Using$( i )$ in above equation,

cos\theta = $\dfrac{n^{2} - 1}{1 + n^{2}}$

\theta = \cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{n^{2} - 1}{n^{2} + 1}\right)$

questions.q: In the density measurement of a cube, the mass and edge length are measured as \left(10.00 \pm 0.10\right)kg$ and \left(0.10 \pm 0.01\right)m,$ respectively. The error in the measurement of density is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$Density \left(ρ\right) = \dfrac{mass}{volume}$
$\dfrac{∆ ρ}{ρ} = \dfrac{∆ m}{m} + \dfrac{∆ V}{V}$
$= \dfrac{∆ m}{m} + \dfrac{3 ∆ a}{a} \left(∵ V = a^{3}\right)$
=\dfrac{0.1}{10} +$3 \left(\dfrac{0.01}{0.1}\right)$
$= 0.01 + 3 \left(0.1\right)$
$= 0.31$

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Use triangle law of vector addition,&

questions.q: A physical quantity $Q$ is found to depend on quantities $a, b, c$ by the relation $Q = \dfrac{a^{4}b^{3}}{c2}$. The percentage error in $a, b$ and $c$ are $3 % , 4 %$ and $5 %$ respectively. Then, the percentage error in $Q$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given quantity is $Q = \dfrac{a^{4}b^{3}}{c2}$.

The relative error in measuring $Q$ is given by

$\dfrac{\Delta Q}{Q} = 4\dfrac{\Deltaa}{a} + 3\dfrac{\Deltab}{b} + 2\dfrac{\Deltac}{c} . . . \left(1\right)$

Hence, the required percentage error is given by

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{\Delta Q}{Q} \times100 & = & 4\left(\dfrac{\Deltaa}{a} \times100\right) + 3\left(\dfrac{\Deltab}{b} \times100\right) + 2\left(\dfrac{\Deltac}{c} \times100\right) \\ & = & 4 \times3 % + 3 \times4 % + 2 \times5 % \\ & = & 12 % + 12 % + 10 % \\ & = & 34 %\end{cases}$

questions.q: If $\overset{→}{A}$ and $\overset{→}{B}$ are two vectors satisfying the relation~$\overset{→}{A} \cdot \overset{→}{B} = | \overset{→}{A} \times \overset{→}{B} |$. Then the value of $| \overset{→}{A} - \overset{→}{B} |$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{A} \cdot \overset{→}{B} = | \overset{→}{A} \times \overset{→}{B} |$
$ABcos \theta = ABsin \theta ⇒ \theta = 45 °$
$| \overset{→}{A} - \overset{→}{B} | = \sqrt{A^{2} + B^{2} - 2ABcos45 °}$
$= \sqrt{A^{2} + B^{2} - \sqrt{2}AB}$
Hence option $( 4 ) .$

Area of square $= 5.29cm^{2}$

questions.solution:
Volume of the wire is& $V = \pir^{2}l$.

Density of the wire is~$ρ = \dfrac{m}{\pir^{2}l}$

Relative error in measurement of density

$⇒ \dfrac{\Deltaρ}{ρ} = \dfrac{\Deltam}{m} + 2 \times \dfrac{\Deltar}{r} + \dfrac{\Deltal}{l}$

questions.subject: Physics

$g = \dfrac{4{π}^{2}l}{T2}$

questions.q: In order to determine the Young's Modulus of a wire of radius $0 . 2cm$ (measured using a scale of least count $= 0 . 001cm$) and length $1m$ (measured using a scale of least count $= 1mm$), a weight of mass $1$ kg (measured using a scale of least count $= 1g$ ) was hanged to get the elongation of $0 . 5cm$ (measured using a scale of least count~$0 . 001cm$). What will be the fractional error in the value of Young's Modulus determined by this experiment?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$Y = \dfrac{Stress}{Strain} = \dfrac{FL}{Al} = \dfrac{mgL}{\piR^{2}l}$

$\dfrac{\Delta Y}{Y} = \dfrac{\Deltam}{m} + \dfrac{\Delta L}{L} + 2\dfrac{\Delta R}{R} + \dfrac{Δl}{l}$

$\dfrac{\Delta Y}{Y} \times 100 = 100 \left[\dfrac{1}{1000} + \dfrac{1}{1000} +$2\left(\dfrac{0 . 001}{0 . 2}\right) + \dfrac{0 . 001}{0 . 5}\right]

=\dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{10} +$1 + $\dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{14}{10} =$1 . 4 %$

questions.q: The resistance $R = \dfrac{V}{I}$, where $V = ( 200 \pm 5 ) V$ and $I = ( 20 \pm 0 . 2 ) A$, the percentage error in the measurement of $R$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that, $R = \dfrac{V}{I}$

According to error analysis

$\dfrac{dR}{R} = \dfrac{dV}{V} + \dfrac{dI}{I} ⇒ \dfrac{dR}{R} = \dfrac{5}{200} + \dfrac{0 . 2}{20} ⇒ \dfrac{dR}{R} = \dfrac{7}{200}$

Thus, the percentage error can be calculated as follows:

$% \text{error} = \dfrac{dR}{R} \times 100 = \dfrac{7}{200} \times 100 = 3 . 5 %$

questions.q: Two resistance are given as ${R}_{1} = ( 10 \pm 0 . 5 ) Ω$~and ${R}_{2} = ( 15 \pm 0 . 5 ) Ω .$ The percentage error in the measurement of equivalent resistance when they are connected in parallel is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Equivalent resistance in parallel combination is given by
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{R_{\text {eq }}}=\frac{1}{R_1}+\frac{1}{R_2} \\
& \Rightarrow R_{\text {eq }}=\frac{R_1 R_2}{R_1+R_2}=\frac{10 \times 15}{10+15}=6
\end{aligned}$
Differentiating both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{\Delta R_{\text {eq }}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}^2}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_1}{\mathrm{R}_1^2}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_2^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\left(\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_1}{\mathrm{R}_1^2}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_2^2}\right) \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}} \\ & =\left(\frac{0.5}{100}+\frac{0.5}{225}\right) \cdot 6=\left(\frac{6 \times 0.5}{25}\right)\left(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{9}\right)=\frac{13}{300} \\ & \frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}} \times 100=\frac{13}{3}=4.33 \%\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The maximum error in the measurement of resistance, current and time for which current flows in an electrical circuit are $1 % , 2 %$ and $3 %$ respectively. The maximum percentage error in the detection of the dissipated heat will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Heat generated through resistance is given by,& $H = i^{2}Rt$

Therefore, the percentage error in the calculation can be found by,

$⇒ \dfrac{\Delta H}{H} \times 100 = 2 \times \dfrac{\Deltai}{i} \times 100 + \dfrac{\Delta R}{R} \times 100 + \dfrac{\Deltat}{t} \times 100$

$⇒ \dfrac{\Delta H}{H} \times 100 = 4 % + 1 % + 3 %$

$⇒ \dfrac{\Delta H}{H} \times 100 = 8 %$

questions.q: If the percentage errors in measuring the length and the diameter of a wire are $0 . 1 %$ each. The percentage error in measuring its resistance will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resistance of the wire in terms of the diameter can be written as, $R = \dfrac{ρL}{\pi\dfrac{d2}{4}}$

Hence, percentage error relation will be, $\dfrac{∆ R}{R} \times 100 = \dfrac{∆ L}{L} \times 100 + \dfrac{2 ∆ d}{d} \times 100$

Given: $\dfrac{∆ L}{L} = 0 . 1 %$ and $\dfrac{∆ d}{d} = 0 . 1 %$

Therefore, $\dfrac{∆ R}{R} = 0 . 3 %$

questions.q: If the projection of $2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ on $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \alpha\overset{^}{k}$ is zero. Then, the value of $\alpha$ will be

questions.q: In an experiment of measuring the refractive index of a glass slab using travelling microscope in physics lab, a student measures real thickness of the glass slab as $5 . 25mm$ and apparent thickness of the glass slab at $5 . 00mm$. Travelling microscope has $20$ divisions in one $cm$ on main scale and $50$ divisions on Vernier scale is equal to $49$ divisions on main scale. The estimated uncertainty in the measurement of refractive index of the slab is~$\dfrac{x}{10} \times {10}^{- 3}$, where~$x$& is ______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:&

$50VSD = 49MSD ⇒ 1VSD = \dfrac{49}{50}MSD$

So least count will be

$= 1MSD - 1VSD = \dfrac{1}{20}cm - \dfrac{49}{50} \cdot \dfrac{1}{20}cm$

$= \dfrac{1}{50} \times \dfrac{1}{20}cm = 0 . 01mm$

As we know,~$\mu = \dfrac{h}{h '} = \dfrac{5 . 25}{5 . 00}$

Applying log on both sides, we get

$ln\mu = lnh – lnh ’$

Differentiating both sides, we get

$\dfrac{d\mu}{μ} = \dfrac{dh}{h} - \dfrac{dh '}{h '}$

For calculation, all errors will be added, therefore

$d\mu = \left[\dfrac{0 . 01}{5 . 25} + \dfrac{0 . 01}{5 . 00}\right]\mu$

$= \dfrac{41}{10} \times {10}^{- 3}$

Hence,~$x = 41$
